title: Adaptive jittered flush and downstream-aware credit pacing for smoother streaming
author: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Implements three coordinated runtime changes to reduce streaming tail and burst latency for token-generation workloads: (1) a jittered flush window that spreads microbatch flushes to avoid aligned burst tails; (2) a downstream-latency-aware credit allocator that paces token credits based on observed consumer RTT and in-flight decode headroom; (3) a speculative KV prefix hint prefetch that warms per-GPU KV cache for likely next-token prefixes using a lightweight in-memory prefix index. Goal: smooth token emission, reduce 95/99p TTFB for streaming clients, and avoid unnecessary kernel wakeups while keeping median latency neutral. Motivation and context: Production canaries and incidents (ENG-4823, ENG-4899) showed recurring tail spikes when many concurrent streams synchronized flushes at token boundaries or periodic intervals. Prior PRs mitigated parts of this, but correlation remained across streams, producing CPU/GPU contention and simultaneous KV cache churn. This change targets coordination between emitter, scheduler, and KV hinting to reduce correlated bursts without increasing steady-state cost. Design: JitteredFlushWindow: each emitter derives a small per-request jitter from request id + start time; flushes are randomized inside a window with an adaptive slack that shrinks when congestion is low. RTT-aware CreditPacer: credits are paced using a moving estimate of downstream RTT (transport/ACK hooks). Allocator reduces burst credits when downstream latency rises and opportunistically issues larger credits when downstream is responsive and batch headroom exists. KV Speculative Hints: maintain a light-weight probabilistic prefix index populated from recent prompts and frequent token transitions; when high-confidence candidates exist, schedule a low-cost prefetch of relevant KV pages into the local per-GPU cache before the microbatch reaches its max tokens. Prefetching uses a shared budget and is disabled under high cache pressure. Implementation notes and safety knobs: jitter default 20ms ±10ms; adaptive slack 0..50ms controlled by --emit.jitter-slack-ms. CreditPacer exposes --emit.credit-min, --emit.credit-max, --emit.credit-rtt-scale; pacing never increases credits above configured max. KV prefetch is feature-flagged and per-GPU budgeted; disabled on Dedicated/Private by default. Observability: per-request jitter offset, credit decisions, prefetch hits/misses, and cache pressure metrics emitted to metrics pipeline and console. Benchmarks (canary): aggregate micro-canary across 8 r5g instances plus GPU pool with 5k steady concurrent streams showed: 95p TTFB improved ~18% (220ms -> 180ms), 99p improved ~26% (410ms -> 305ms), median ~+2% (neutral). Kernel wakeups at flush boundaries down ~33%. KV cache cold-miss rate for warmed prefixes down ~45%. Rollout plan: Step 1: canary enable JitteredFlushWindow + CreditPacer; KV prefetch disabled. Step 2: enable KV prefetch in canary with low cache pressure and monitor two weeks. Step 3: staged rollout to host pools with metrics-driven gating (require 95p improvement and no error rate increases). Emergency revert: runtime flag --emit.disable-global disables the new behavior instantly. Tests and checklist: unit tests for jitter and credit pacing; integration tests with synthetic slow readers; load canary results uploaded to Linear ENG-4823; metrics and debug traces added; feature flags and knobs available for staged rollout. Commits summary (high level): feat(emitter): add JitteredFlushWindow and config knobs; feat(scheduler): plumb RTT signals to credit allocator and implement CreditPacer; feat(kv): add PrefixHintIndex and speculative prefetch path; test: unit + integration tests; ci: canary pipeline job for end-to-end streaming validation. Changed areas (high level): runtime/emit/emitter.go, runtime/scheduler/credit_pacer.go, runtime/kv/prefix_hint_index.go, runtime/kv/prefetch_manager.go, api/gateway/transport_hooks.go, observability/metrics/emit_metrics.go, test/integration/stream_slow_reader_test.go. Small illustrative snippet (emitter jitter calc): old: flushAt = lastEmit + flushInterval ; new: jitter = (hash(req.id) % jitterWindow) - jitterWindow/2 ; flushAt = lastEmit + flushInterval + jitter + adaptiveSlack. Review summary: reviewers raised concerns about rate-limit interactions and Dedicated memory pressure; addressed by ensuring jitter never reduces credits below configured minima, adding tests for rate-limit invariants, disabling KV prefetch on Dedicated/Private by default, adding per-GPU budgeting and LRU eviction cap. Metric naming nit (emit.jitter_offset_ms -> emit.jitter_offset_millis) fixed. CI summary: unit: pass; integration: pass; lint: pass; canary-sim: pass; total: pass. Merge: squash-merge to main by Mateo Ruiz referencing ENG-4823 and ENG-4899. Release notes: Adaptive jittered flush and downstream-aware credit pacing reduce streaming tail latency (95/99p); optional KV speculative prefetch warms high-confidence prefixes; opt-in via runtime flags; staged rollout performed. Notes: favors smoothing over aggressive micro-optimizations; follow-ups planned to combine with kernel coalescing heuristics and workload-aware batching.
